bibl.title: A Circle of Egyptian Bishops at the End of Roman Rule (c. 600). Texts and Contexts.
bibl.seg: Phil Booth, A Circle of Egyptian Bishops at the End of Roman Rule (c. 600). Texts and Contexts.
bibl.note: 1. Introduction. - 2. Damian of Alexandria. - 3. John of Paralos. - 4. Constantine of Assiut. - 5. Rufus of Shotep. - 6. John of Hermopolis. - 7. Pesynthius of Koptos. - 8. Abraham of Hermonthis. - 9. Towards the Coptic Church. - 10. Conclusion. - Explores the bishops' need both to legitimise and to distinguish their new Church in the face of Chalcedonian competition, which resulted, among other things, in elevating Coptic as their chosen medium of expression.
